questions.q: Which training method involves alternating periods of intense work and active recovery?
questions.explanation: Interval training uses strict work-to-rest ratios.
It involves playing with speed based on feel.

questions.q: What is the primary physiological purpose of a warm-up?
options: To increase core body temperature and blood flow
questions.explanation: Warm muscles perform better and are less prone to injury.

options: Clear lactic acid and prevent blood pooling
questions.explanation: Cooling down helps the body return to its resting state safely.

questions.q: Running at a steady, moderate pace for 45 minutes without stopping is an example of:
questions.explanation: Continuous training has no rest breaks.

questions.q: The principle of 'Overload' states that to improve fitness, an athlete must:
options: Train exactly the same way every day
Work harder than their body is accustomed to
questions.explanation: Adaptation occurs when the body is stressed beyond normal limits.

questions.q: The principle of 'Reversibility' is often summarized as:
options: Slow and steady wins the race
questions.explanation: Fitness gains are lost if training stops.

questions.q: Performing a series of different exercises at stations with minimal rest between them is called:
questions.explanation: Circuits train multiple systems in a structured loop.
